# Saral DeepEval RAG baseline (golden RAG v2, dev split)

**Label: automated (LLM-judged, no human review).** Every number was produced by the run described in §9 and read from its output files. Retrieval ran on Kaggle (2x T4, no LLM there). Answers were generated by `antigravity/claude-sonnet-4-6` and judged by `codex/gpt-6-luna`, both called through OmniRoute from the Hark sandbox (fallback for either: `gpt-5.6-terra`). The judge is an LLM; judge-human agreement has not been measured yet, so treat this as a first automated baseline.

Date: 2026-11-03/04 (IST). Branch `feat/saral-deepeval-baseline` (base `3de95b0`, the corpus branch).

## 4. Abstain / refuse / clarify correctness (behaviour items)

Judge = DeepEval GEval `ExpectedBehaviour` (rubric in provenance.json). Deterministic = refuse/abstain: the agent declined (abstained or a guard template fired); clarify: the answer contains a question mark.

| Expected | Items | Judge scored | Judge mean | Judge pass @0.5 | Deterministic rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| refuse | 10 | 10 | 0.870 | 1.000 | 0.900 |
| abstain | 8 | 8 | 0.863 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| clarify | 11 | 11 | 0.282 | 0.091 | 0.000 |
| answer_note | 11 | 11 | 0.709 | 1.000 | — |

Generator paths: {'llm': 171, 'boundary:other_applicant': 1, 'boundary:guarantee': 1, 'boundary:injection': 2, 'boundary:edit_record': 2, 'boundary:misrepresentation': 1} (`boundary:*` = the agent's deterministic guard template, `fallback_template` = flagged twice by the agent's answer/citation guards, so the policy_abstain template was used).

## 6. Failures by category

116 of 178 dev items carry at least one failure tag.

| Failure tag | Items | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| leaked_term | 91 | internal term in the answer (regex: OCR, ZEN, RAG, LLM, P1-P5, bureau, chunk, passage, retrieval, embedding, system prompt) |
| retrieval_miss_chunk_only | 14 | gold document retrieved, but not the anchored chunk |
| discrepancy_not_noted | 10 | conflict item (answer_note) with ExpectedBehaviour < 1.0 |
| retrieval_miss | 10 | no gold document in the final top 5 |
| no_clarifying_question | 10 | clarify item with ExpectedBehaviour < 0.5 |
| over_abstain | 3 | abstained (or fell back to the abstain template) on an answerable question |

Golden categories with the most failing items: fees_bounce (3), eligibility_credit_score (3), purpose_wedding (2), purpose_limits (2), tax_interest (2), purpose_medical_emergency (2), amount_min (2), amount_max (2), eligibility_age (2), eligibility_income (2), dl_cooling_off (2), fees_penal (2).

## 8. Limitations (automated)

Built from this run's failures only; counts are dev items (an item can sit in more than one group). Example ids are golden-set ids (synthetic questions, no PII). The likely causes are my reading of the failing items, not a measured attribution.

| Group | Items | Examples | What counts | Likely cause |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Retrieval misses | 24 | R2-AMT-02, R2-DIS-04 | answerable item whose anchored chunk is not in the final top 5 (10 with no gold document at all) | Reranked top 5 favours sibling chunks or a neighbouring document: for R2-AMT-02 (minimum amount) the rates-and-fees page was outranked by overview/eligibility pages; for R2-DLR-05 (delete my data) Bajaj's privacy/app T&C outranked the RBI consumer-finance direction. No collection router, and both collections compete for 5 slots. Most misses still answered correctly from a sibling chunk (Faithfulness stayed 1.0). |
| Unfaithful or unsupported claims | 5 | R2-DLR-01, R2-GRV-06 | Faithfulness < 0.85 (0 below 0.5) | Over-strong paraphrase of qualified policy text: 'up to 36%' stated as exactly 36% (R2-LHR-05), exceptions dropped in the digital-lending disbursal rule (R2-DLR-01), 'dropline limit' turned into 'outstanding limit' (R2-PRE-05). No figure was invented outright in the 149 judged answers. |
| Wrong abstain or refuse | 13 | R2-CLA-01, R2-CLA-02 | over-abstained on an answerable item (3), refuse/abstain item judged wrong (0), clarify item with no clarifying question (10) | Clarify items: the policy prompt has no instruction to ask a clarifying question, and the intent classifier/clarify logic of the full agent was not exercised, so 10 of 11 vague questions got a direct answer (e.g. R2-CLA-03, R2-CLA-08). Over-abstain: the deterministic request guards fire on benign policy questions: 'my friend and I took the same loan' -> other_applicant (R2-RAT-07) and 'credit guarantee scheme fee' -> guarantee (R2-FEE-08); R2-PUR-01 abstained because no passage states per-purpose limits. All 10 refuse and 8 abstain items were handled acceptably by the judge's rubric. |
| Hindi and Telugu failures | 8 | R2-LHI-03, R2-LHI-06 | hi/te item with a failure tag (other than leaked labels) or a metric below its bar (hi 4/9, te 4/11; wrong script: 0) | No wrong-script answers (20/20 in the right script). The few hi/te failures are the same causes as English: a retrieval miss on the RBI-IOS FAQ (R2-LHI-06), a qualified '36%' stated flatly (R2-LHR-05), and conflict notes not made (R2-LHI-03). Samples are small (9 hi, 11 te). |
| Conflict-note handling | 10 | R2-AMT-01, R2-AMT-03 | answer_note (conflicting-source) item with ExpectedBehaviour < 1.0, of 11 such items | The POLICY prompt asks to flag [historical] passages but not to surface disagreeing current sources, so the model gives one figure (e.g. ₹75 lakh in R2-AMT-01) without noting the ₹55 lakh conflict; 10 of 11 answer_note items were scored below 1.0. |
| Latency or rate-limit fallbacks | 1 | R2-LTE-04 | generator fell back to gpt-5.6-terra on 0 items []; generator gave no answer on 0; judge fell back on 1 metric calls (1 items); agent guard fallback template on 0 items; Groq calls: 0; generation latency per item p50 7.69 s, p95 15.38 s, max 22.28 s (OmniRoute, includes the agent's one rewrite when it happened) | No Groq call is made in this eval (OmniRoute stand-ins), so the Groq-to-OmniRoute fallback never fired. Judge stalls happened when in-flight OmniRoute calls hung after sandbox suspension; the judge was re-run in resumable chunks with a 60 s client timeout, and one metric call fell back to gpt-5.6-terra. |
| Internal labels shown to the borrower (also observed) | 91 | R2-ABS-02, R2-ABS-05 | answer text contains an internal term or passage label (leak regex) | The policy prompt asks for citations as P1..P5 labels, and the model also writes them (and the word 'passages') into the answer text; the agent's citation pipeline maps labels to sources but nothing strips them from the prose. Mostly 'passages'/'P1'; 4 answers say 'bureau'. |

**What this eval does not cover:**

- The full LangGraph agent: intent classification, explain / improve / what-if answers, ZEN decisions, tool calls and multi-turn memory (Golden B, agent_v1, is not run here).
- The production generator (gpt-oss-120b on Groq), voice channel, low/high literacy styles, streaming and latency of the real API.
- The 49 held-out RAG items and the 30-item human calibration (no judge-human agreement yet).
- Retrieval against the deployed Qdrant/query encoder on InstaBox; the index here was rebuilt on Kaggle.
- Citation quality beyond the deterministic checks (the citation and figure GEval rubrics were not run in this baseline), and the deterministic ungrounded-number guard.
- PII handling, prompt-injection inside retrieved passages, and other applicants' data beyond the few behaviour items.

## 10. Caveats

- Kaggle ran RAG only (embedding, indexing, retrieval, reranking) and wrote per-item retrieved contexts with ids and scores (retrieved_contexts.jsonl, sha256 recorded in run_meta.json). No LLM ran on Kaggle (user directive, 2026-11-04 00:06 IST). An earlier kernel version that served vLLM models, and a leftover v1 judge kernel, were cancelled before producing results.
- Generator antigravity/claude-sonnet-4-6 and judge codex/gpt-6-luna were called through OmniRoute from the Hark sandbox (≤4 concurrent, retries with backoff); fallback for either is gpt-5.6-terra, and every item or metric call that used it is listed. Production uses openai/gpt-oss-120b on Groq; Sonnet stands in for it here, so answer quality is not the production model's. No Groq call was made in this eval, so the Groq-to-OmniRoute fallback never fired.
- Generation emulates the agent's policy path (deterministic request guards -> boundary templates; prompts.POLICY in the item's language, literacy medium, text channel; answer + citation guards with one rewrite; policy_abstain fallback). Not emulated: the LLM intent classifier (every item is treated as a policy question), the ungrounded-number guard, streaming and Langfuse. Clarify items therefore show what the policy path does, not the full LangGraph agent.
- Retrieval rebuilds the index in the kernel from the same cleaned chunks (EmbeddingGemma-2 in float32 because T4 has no bf16; G1 indexed in bf16 on CPU), so vectors can differ slightly from the qdrant_v3 copy. Each question searches both collections; the union is cut to the top 5 by reranker score (the repo has no router yet).
- Golden v2 is release candidate saral_golden_v2.0-rc1, frontier-authored, review_status pending_human. Only the 178 dev items were shipped and run. The 49 held-out items were never uploaded, and the eval script aborts if a held-out id appears.
- The judge is an LLM (codex/gpt-6-luna). Judge-human agreement has not been measured; the 30 calibration items in PR #44 exist for that. Hindi and Telugu samples are small (9 hi, 11 te dev items), so per-language numbers are indicative only.
- Each judge metric is tried at most twice; failures are recorded as unscored, never as a score.
- The judge ran in resumable chunks (the sandbox suspends background work between steps), so judge_info.json 'seconds' covers only the last chunk; every metric was scored exactly once in the final file (636 jobs, 0 errors).
